originality.rationale: Arvind et al. (arXiv:1502.01255) provide the general logic/refinability framework, but not this sharp finite abelian Cayley minimum. Kluge (arXiv:2204.01054), full Section 4, proves the prime cyclic case and exhibits a sixteen-vertex abelian failure; the result does not prove the all-abelian lower bound for groups of orders 1 through 15. The present contribution is the exact exclusion of every smaller abelian Cayley connection set, not discovery of the witness. Actual published-finding corpus and literature searches found no equivalent or stronger cutoff; specialized prior tabulation remains a risk.
residual_risks: An earlier small-order exhaustive abelian Cayley census or an uninspected theorem may imply the same cutoff; independent publication priority is unverified.
The science is a bounded finite classification; it does not imply corresponding results at larger graph orders or after further individualization.

value.rationale: The minimum abelian Cayley order at which one-point refinement can split more coarsely than rooted automorphism orbits is a natural sharp boundary prompted by Kluge’s explicit size-sixteen example. Lower-order examples cannot be dismissed from prime-group theory alone because many smaller abelian groups are composite/noncyclic; exhaustive 821-case proof gives a reusable exact lower-bound certificate and records the first failure. This is a motivated finite cutoff, not a trivial restatement of a known witness.
